items.title: Federal Cannabis Reform in 2026: Why Industry Leaders Call It a Tailwind, Not a Lifeline
items.summary: Federal cannabis reform in 2026 is gaining measurable momentum, but industry leaders caution that rescheduling and safe banking are not immediate solutions for operators. At IgniteIt’s New Jersey Spotlight panel, Nabis CEO Vince C. Ning joined capital markets and policy experts to break down what federal cannabis rescheduling, safe banking legislation, hemp regulation, and interstate commerce could realistically mean for licensed operators. While the potential shift from Schedule I to Schedule III could ease 280E tax burdens, panelists emphasized that regulatory clarity, IRS interpretation, and implementation timelines will determine real impact. Discussions also highlighted how federal cannabis policy is evolving from plant-based frameworks toward cannabinoid-centric regulation, signaling structural change across compliance, packaging, and interstate distribution. The takeaway: federal cannabis reform represents a long-term tailwind for the industry, not a short-term lifeline. For operators navigating compliance risk, capital constraints, and market volatility, disciplined fundamentals remain essential as Washington’s policy landscape continues to evolve.
